text:
maria: Quick sync — ACME asked for per-tenant isolation + cross-region failover by EoY. Can we scope that for Q4? @eng-platform @sales
aj: short answer: possible but we need to pick an isolation model. options: soft slices (routing affinity + quotas) vs hard slices (dedicated capacity). tradeoffs: cost, ops complexity.
kevin: data residency + KMS for cross-region will add 2–3 sprints if this goes into Private.
sophia: propose phased approach:
- phase 0: routing policy DSL + region affinity algos (low risk)
- phase 1: tenant slices + soft isolation (quotas, throttles, per-tenant caching rules)
- phase 2: hard isolation (dedicated lanes, reserved capacity, billing)
luis: agree. suggested launch criteria per phase:
- p0: DSL expressivity, test harness, route telemetry in prod-sim
- p1: isolation SLOs met in perf env, migration playbook, one pilot customer
- p2: capacity guarantees, SLA language, billing integration + legal signoff
maria: also need customer acceptance tests and rollback plan. @sales please confirm ACME will do canary with us.
aj: eng constraints we should call out: KV cache invalidation patterns, batching behavior across slices, and routing fallback semantics. sample DSL (first pass):
```policy
route {
  match tenant_id /^acme-/
  prefer region us-west-2
  fallback model small-latency
}
```
kevin: ops note: cross-region failover needs state sync for byte-addressable KV cache or we must fallback to stateless variant to avoid big latency cliffs.
sophia: risk register items: compliance (cross-border), billing accuracy, rollout automation. recommend gating each phase with isolation smoke tests + 2 pilot customers before broad launch.
maria: timeline (very rough): p0 = 3 weeks, p1 = 6 weeks, p2 = 8–10 weeks depending on infra deps. can we surface this for the next roadmap review? @cto
luis: +1. I'll book a product-arch sync and collect the acceptance test list.
deploy-bot: scheduled: product-arch-sync on 2024-08-14 16:00 UTC
aj: created RFC-6821 draft for routing policy + migration playbook, will add perf targets and migration steps.
kevin: note to infra capacity planners — need estimates for reserved lanes by EOW.
maria: thanks all — I'll update the roadmap doc and post links here. :thumbsup:
